# By regulation

<!-- This file is generated by scripts/build.py from data/resources/*.yml. Edit the data, not this file. -->

A cross-index of the same entries as [`README.md`](../README.md), grouped by the
instrument that puts them in scope. An entry can appear under more than one
heading, and an entry that appears under none is still in scope through its
maintainer rather than through a specific regulation.

## NIS2

*Directive (EU) 2022/2555* - 10 entries

- [anssi-nis2](https://github.com/betagouv/anssi-nis2) - Source code behind ANSSI's public platform guiding French entities through NIS2 Directive applicability and their resulting obligations. 🇫🇷 `France/ANSSI` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>
- [ENISA Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Policies in the EU](https://www.enisa.europa.eu/publications/coordinated-vulnerability-disclosure-policies-in-the-eu) - ENISA study mapping national coordinated vulnerability disclosure policies across Member States, with recommendations later reflected in NIS2 and CRA disclosure duties. 🇪🇺 `EU/ENISA` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [ENISA NIS360](https://www.enisa.europa.eu/enisa-nis360-2026) - Annual ENISA report assessing the cybersecurity maturity and criticality of the sectors of high criticality listed in Annex I of the NIS2 Directive. 🇪🇺 `EU/ENISA` <sub>Threat Intelligence</sub>
- [EU-CyCLONe](https://www.enisa.europa.eu/topics/eu-incident-response-and-cyber-crisis-management/eu-cyclone) - The EU Cyber Crisis Liaison Organisation Network formalised by NIS2 Article 16, through which ENISA supports Member State crisis authorities with shared situational awareness. 🇪🇺 `EU/ENISA` <sub>Threat Intelligence</sub>
- [Greek National Cybersecurity Authority](https://cyber.gov.gr/en/) - Greece's national cybersecurity authority, responsible for NIS2 regulatory oversight, incident coordination and requirements for essential and important entities. 🇬🇷 `Greece/NCSA` <sub>National Cybersecurity Authorities & Standards</sub>
- [Ireland NCSC NIS2 Guidance](https://www.ncsc.gov.ie/nis2/) - Ireland's NCSC hub for NIS2 transposition guidance, including draft risk-management measures, a scope self-assessment tool and its recommendation of the CyFun framework. 🇮🇪 `Ireland/NCSC` <sub>National Cybersecurity Authorities & Standards</sub>
- [NIS2 Scope and Awareness Resources](https://www.enisa.europa.eu/topics/awareness-and-cyber-hygiene/raising-awareness-campaigns/network-and-information-systems-directive-2-nis2) - ENISA provides implementation-oriented NIS2 scope, obligations, and awareness resources for covered entities. 🇪🇺 `EU/ENISA` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>
- [NIS2 Technical Implementation Guidance](https://www.enisa.europa.eu/publications/nis2-technical-implementation-guidance) - ENISA guidance translates the NIS2 implementing act into technical cybersecurity risk-management measures. 🇪🇺 `EU/ENISA` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>
- [nis2-public](https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/nis2-public) - This open-source repository provides NIS2-oriented posture-management controls and reporting. 🇮🇹 `Italy/Community` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>
- [verinice](https://github.com/SerNet/verinice) - Open-source ISMS and GRC platform implementing BSI IT-Grundschutz and ISO 27001, with modules covering NIS2 and GDPR compliance. 🇩🇪 `Germany/SerNet` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>

## DORA

*Regulation (EU) 2022/2554* - 22 entries

- [Central Bank of Ireland DORA Incident Reporting](https://www.centralbank.ie/regulation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora/reporting-major-ict-related-incidents-and-significant-cyber-threats) - National guidance and templates for DORA major ICT-incident and significant-cyber-threat reporting by financial entities supervised in Ireland. 🇮🇪 `Ireland/Central Bank of Ireland` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [DNB Good Practice Information Security](https://www.dnb.nl/media/13jpibjp/good-practice-ib-2023-eng.pdf) - De Nederlandsche Bank supervisory good-practice document setting information-security control expectations aligned with the DORA ICT risk-management requirements. 🇳🇱 `Netherlands/DNB` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [DORA Incident Classification RTS](https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2024-01/JC_2023_83_-_Final_Report_on_draft_RTS_on_classification_of_major_incidents_and_significant_cyber_threats.pdf) - The joint ESA standard defines criteria for classifying major ICT incidents and significant cyber threats under DORA. 🇪🇺 `EU/ESAs` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [DORA Major Incident Reporting RTS and ITS](https://www.eba.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2023-12/ecc72f1c-c68a-4e64-97dd-47470117c3ae/JC%202023%2070%20-%20%20CP%20on%20draft%20RTS%20and%20ITS%20on%20major%20incident%20reporting%20under%20DORA.pdf) - The joint ESA package specifies DORA major-incident reporting content, timelines, and templates. 🇪🇺 `EU/ESAs` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [DORA Register of Information ITS](https://www.eba.europa.eu/activities/single-rulebook/regulatory-activities/operational-resilience/implementing-technical-standards-establish-templates-register-information) - The EBA page publishes implementing technical standards for DORA registers of contractual ICT arrangements. 🇪🇺 `EU/EBA` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [DORA Registers of Information Templates](https://www.eba.europa.eu/activities/direct-supervision-and-oversight/digital-operational-resilience-act/preparation-dora-application) - The European Supervisory Authorities provide templates for DORA ICT third-party registers of information. 🇪🇺 `EU/ESAs` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [DORA TLPT Regulatory Technical Standards](https://www.eba.europa.eu/activities/single-rulebook/regulatory-activities/operational-resilience/joint-regulatory-technical-standards-specifying-elements-related-threat-led-penetration-tests) - The joint ESA standard specifies DORA requirements for threat-led penetration testing. 🇪🇺 `EU/ESAs` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [EBA Reporting Framework 3.5](https://www.eba.europa.eu/risk-and-data-analysis/reporting/reporting-frameworks/reporting-framework-35) - EBA technical package of data point model, XBRL taxonomy and validation rules implementing the cross-sectoral DORA register-of-information reporting requirements. 🇪🇺 `EU/EBA` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [EIOPA DORA Hub](https://www.eiopa.europa.eu/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora_en) - EIOPA landing page consolidating DORA implementation material, technical standards and oversight information for the insurance and pensions sector. 🇪🇺 `EU/EIOPA` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [ESAs Designation of Critical ICT Third-Party Providers](https://www.eiopa.europa.eu/european-supervisory-authorities-designate-critical-ict-third-party-providers-under-digital-2025-11-18_en) - Joint announcement by the European Supervisory Authorities naming the first ICT providers designated as critical under the DORA oversight framework. 🇪🇺 `EU/ESAs` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [ESAs FAQ on Registers of Information](https://www.eba.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2025-03/31bb6e60-7d10-4405-a8c5-9f04934630ac/20250328%20-%20DORA%20RoI%20reporting%20FAQ%20(updated).pdf) - ESAs FAQ answering practical questions on preparing and submitting DORA registers of information under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956. 🇪🇺 `EU/ESAs` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [ESAs Guidelines on Aggregated Costs and Losses](https://www.eba.europa.eu/activities/single-rulebook/regulatory-activities/operational-resilience/joint-guidelines-estimation-aggregated-annual-costs-and-losses-caused-major-ict-related-incidents) - ESAs joint guidelines harmonising how DORA-covered financial entities estimate and report aggregated annual costs and losses from major ICT incidents. 🇪🇺 `EU/ESAs` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [ESMA DORA Oversight](https://www.esma.europa.eu/dora-oversight) - ESMA's page describing the joint ESAs oversight regime for critical ICT third-party providers designated under DORA. 🇪🇺 `EU/ESMA` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [EU Systemic Cyber Incident Coordination Framework](https://www.eiopa.europa.eu/esas-establish-framework-strengthen-coordination-case-systemic-cyber-incidents-2024-07-17_en) - ESAs framework establishing a pan-European coordination mechanism for major cyber incidents with systemic potential in the financial sector under DORA. 🇪🇺 `EU/ESAs` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [Pandora](https://github.com/pandora-analysis/pandora) - Analysis framework from CIRCL Luxembourg that inspects submitted files with multiple integrated tools to determine whether they are suspicious or malicious. 🇱🇺 `Luxembourg/CIRCL` <sub>Threat Intelligence</sub>
- [TIBER-BE](https://www.nbb.be/en/financial-supervision-and-resolution/digital-resilience-and-cyber-risk/tiber-be-team) - National Bank of Belgium's TIBER-EU implementation, coordinating controlled threat-led red-team tests for Belgian financial institutions under DORA. 🇧🇪 `Belgium/NBB` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [TIBER-DE](https://www.bundesbank.de/en/tasks/payment-systems/tiber-de/tiber-de-817014) - Deutsche Bundesbank's national TIBER-EU implementation, run with BaFin, used by German financial entities for DORA-mandated threat-led penetration tests. 🇩🇪 `Germany/Bundesbank` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [TIBER-EU Framework 2025](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/pub/pdf/other/ecb.tiber_eu_framework_2025~b32eff9a10.en.pdf) - The ECB framework defines intelligence-led red-team testing aligned with DORA TLPT requirements. 🇪🇺 `EU/ECB` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [TIBER-EU Purple Teaming Guidance](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/pub/pdf/annex/ecb.tiber_eu_purple_best_practices_2025.en.pdf) - ECB guidance on structuring purple-teaming activity inside TIBER-EU and DORA threat-led penetration tests, replacing the 2022 edition. 🇪🇺 `EU/ECB` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [TIBER-IE](https://www.centralbank.ie/financial-system/operational-resilience-and-cyber/cyber-resilience/tiber-ie) - Central Bank of Ireland's national TIBER-EU programme coordinating intelligence-led red-team tests that Irish financial entities use to meet DORA TLPT obligations. 🇮🇪 `Ireland/Central Bank of Ireland` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [TIBER-IT](https://www.consob.it/web/consob-and-its-activities/tiber-it-national-guidance) - Joint CONSOB, Banca d'Italia and IVASS guidance hosting the TIBER-IT national guide used by Italian financial entities for DORA threat-led penetration tests. 🇮🇹 `Italy/CONSOB` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>
- [TIBER-NL](https://www.dnb.nl/en/sector-information/cash-and-payment-systems/dnb-oversees-cyber-resilience-tests/threat-intelligence-based-ethical-red-teaming-tiber/) - De Nederlandsche Bank's national implementation of TIBER-EU, used by Dutch financial entities to satisfy the DORA threat-led penetration testing requirement. 🇳🇱 `Netherlands/DNB` <sub>Financial Sector Resilience (DORA)</sub>

## Cyber Resilience Act

*Regulation (EU) 2024/2847* - 21 entries

- [BSI Cyber Resilience Act Guidance](https://www.bsi.bund.de/EN/Themen/Unternehmen-und-Organisationen/Informationen-und-Empfehlungen/Cyber_Resilience_Act/cyber_resilience_act.html) - BSI guidance explains operational product-security obligations under the EU Cyber Resilience Act. 🇩🇪 `Germany/BSI` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [BSI TR-03183 Cyber Resilience Requirements](https://www.bsi.bund.de/EN/Themen/Unternehmen-und-Organisationen/Standards-und-Zertifizierung/Technische-Richtlinien/TR-nach-Thema-sortiert/tr03183/tr-03183.html) - BSI technical guideline specifying the SBOM, vulnerability-reporting and conformity requirements that operationalise the EU Cyber Resilience Act for manufacturers. 🇩🇪 `Germany/BSI` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup Instance](https://vulnerability.circl.lu/) - Public instance run by CIRCL Luxembourg for searching and correlating vulnerability advisories from national databases, CSAF feeds and community sightings. 🇱🇺 `Luxembourg/CIRCL` <sub>Threat Intelligence</sub>
- [CRA Article 14 Reporting Kit](https://github.com/stavenor-hq/cra-article-14-reporting-kit) - Openly licensed reference files for the EU Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligations of Article 14, covering the filing deadlines, the fields of ENISA's Single Reporting Platform and a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy template. 🇮🇹 `Italy/Stavenor` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [CRA Brief Guide for Open Source Developers](https://best.openssf.org/CRA-Brief-Guide-for-OSS-Developers.html) - OpenSSF guide explaining, against the EU Cyber Resilience Act text, when individual open-source contributors rather than commercial manufacturers fall under the Regulation. 🇪🇺 `International/OpenSSF` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [CRA Conformity Assessment Guidance](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cra-conformity-assessment) - The Commission guidance explains CRA conformity-assessment routes for products with digital elements. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [CSAF Distribution Toolset](https://github.com/gocsaf/csaf) - Go toolset originally built for Germany's BSI implementing a CSAF trusted provider, downloader, validator and aggregator for publishing vulnerability advisories. 🇩🇪 `Germany/BSI` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [CSAF Validator Service](https://github.com/secvisogram/csaf-validator-service) - REST validation service built alongside BSI's Secvisogram that checks CSAF 2.0 documents against the schema used for EU vulnerability advisory publication. 🇩🇪 `Germany/BSI` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [ENISA Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Policies in the EU](https://www.enisa.europa.eu/publications/coordinated-vulnerability-disclosure-policies-in-the-eu) - ENISA study mapping national coordinated vulnerability disclosure policies across Member States, with recommendations later reflected in NIS2 and CRA disclosure duties. 🇪🇺 `EU/ENISA` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [ENISA Single Reporting Platform](https://www.enisa.europa.eu/topics/product-security/single-reporting-platform-srp) - ENISA-operated platform through which manufacturers and open-source stewards submit the Cyber Resilience Act Article 14 vulnerability and incident notifications to CSIRTs. 🇪🇺 `EU/ENISA` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [European Commission CRA Implementation Portal](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-resilience-act) - The Commission portal consolidates implementation material for the EU Cyber Resilience Act, including open-source software considerations. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [European Commission CRA Open Source Guidance](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cra-open-source) - The Commission guidance explains how the CRA applies to free and open-source software and software stewards. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [NCSC-NL Security Advisories CSAF Feed](https://advisories.ncsc.nl/) - NCSC-NL publishes machine-readable CSAF security advisories. 🇳🇱 `Netherlands/NCSC-NL` <sub>Threat Intelligence</sub>
- [OCCTET](https://occtet.eu/) - Digital Europe Programme project coordinated by the Eclipse Foundation building free SBOM, dependency-analysis and compliance-documentation tooling for CRA conformity. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [Open Regulatory Compliance Working Group](https://orcwg.org/) - Eclipse Foundation working group producing community guidance, FAQs and a resource hub to help open-source maintainers meet EU Cyber Resilience Act obligations. 🇪🇺 `EU/Eclipse Foundation` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [ORC WG CRA FAQ](https://cra.orcwg.org/faq/official/assessment/) - The Open Regulatory Compliance Working Group provides implementation guidance for CRA conformity assessment of open-source software. 🇪🇺 `EU/Open Regulatory Compliance Working Group` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [OSS Stewards Obligations Checklist](https://policy.openssf.org/CRA/checklists/OSS_Stewards_Obligations_Checklist.html) - OpenSSF checklist translating the EU Cyber Resilience Act Article 24 open-source steward duties into concrete verifiable compliance steps. 🇪🇺 `International/OpenSSF` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [REUSE](https://reuse.software/) - Tool and specification from the Free Software Foundation Europe for machine-readable SPDX licensing metadata, feeding the bill-of-materials data CRA technical documentation requires. 🇪🇺 `EU/FSFE` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [SBOM for Artificial Intelligence](https://cyber.gouv.fr/nous-connaitre/publications/publications-internationales/software-bill-of-materials-sbom-for-artificial-intelligence/) - ANSSI-published guidance, co-signed with Germany's BSI, defining minimum SBOM elements for AI systems as part of a supply-chain transparency recommendation. 🇫🇷 `France/ANSSI` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [Secvisogram](https://github.com/BSI-Bund/secvisogram) - BSI-maintained web editor for creating and validating CSAF 2.0 and 2.1 security advisories used for coordinated vulnerability disclosure in the EU. 🇩🇪 `Germany/BSI` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>
- [STAN4CRA Standardisation Portal](https://www.stan4cra.eu/) - EU and EFTA-funded portal where CEN, CENELEC and ETSI publish progress on the harmonised standards required for Cyber Resilience Act conformity assessment under mandate M/606. 🇪🇺 `EU/CEN-CENELEC-ETSI` <sub>Software Supply Chain & Product Security (CRA)</sub>

## GDPR

*Regulation (EU) 2016/679* - 6 entries

- [ARX Data Anonymization Tool](https://arx.deidentifier.org/) - Open-source anonymisation tool from the Berlin Institute of Health implementing statistical disclosure control methods used for GDPR anonymisation and pseudonymisation. 🇩🇪 `Germany/Berlin Institute of Health` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>
- [LINDDUN](https://linddun.org/) - Privacy threat modelling framework from KU Leuven that operationalises GDPR privacy-by-design through structured threat categories and mitigation tooling. 🇧🇪 `Belgium/KU Leuven` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>
- [PDP4E Privacy Engineering Toolkit](https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/787034/results) - The EU-funded PDP4E project publishes privacy-engineering methods and tools for implementing GDPR requirements. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>
- [PIA](https://github.com/LINCnil/pia) - Open-source software from the French data protection authority CNIL for conducting GDPR Data Protection Impact Assessments. 🇫🇷 `France/CNIL` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>
- [verinice](https://github.com/SerNet/verinice) - Open-source ISMS and GRC platform implementing BSI IT-Grundschutz and ISO 27001, with modules covering NIS2 and GDPR compliance. 🇩🇪 `Germany/SerNet` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>
- [Website Evidence Collector](https://code.europa.eu/EDPS/website-evidence-collector) - Tool from the European Data Protection Supervisor that automates evidence collection on website storage and transfer of personal data for GDPR inspections. 🇪🇺 `EU/EDPS` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>

## EU AI Act

*Regulation (EU) 2024/1689* - 4 entries

- [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en) - European Commission platform offering an AI Act Explorer and interactive Compliance Checker for determining obligations under the EU AI Act. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>
- [capAI](https://www.oii.ox.ac.uk/a-report-from-the-universities-of-oxford-and-bologna-will-help-protect-society-from-unethical-ai-with-a-world-first-approach-to-support-organisations-to-meet-future-eu-regulations/) - University of Oxford announcement of capAI, a conformity assessment procedure for the EU AI Act developed with the University of Bologna. 🇮🇹 `Italy/University of Bologna` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>
- [COMPL-AI](https://github.com/compl-ai/compl-ai) - Open-source evaluation framework mapping generative AI model benchmarks to EU AI Act requirements, built by ETH Zurich, INSAIT and LatticeFlow AI. 🇨🇭 `Switzerland/ETH Zurich` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>
- [EuConform](https://github.com/Hiepler/EuConform) - EuConform is an open-source tool for documenting and mapping conformity obligations under the EU AI Act. 🇪🇺 `EU/Community` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>

## eIDAS

*Regulation (EU) 910/2014 and 2024/1183* - 25 entries

- [AusweisApp](https://github.com/Governikus/AusweisApp) - Germany's official open-source eID client for authenticating with the national identity card online function, connected to the German eIDAS node. 🇩🇪 `Germany/Governikus` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [Autenticação.gov Middleware](https://github.com/amagovpt/autenticacao.gov) - Portugal's official middleware for the Citizen Card and Chave Móvel Digital, supporting national authentication and qualified signature creation under eIDAS. 🇵🇹 `Portugal/AMA` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [Digital Signature Services (DSS)](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/DIGITAL/pages/467109107/Digital+Signature+Service+-+DSS) - The European Commission's open-source DSS library implements eIDAS-aligned electronic signatures including PAdES. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [DSS Documentation](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/DSS/webapp-demo/doc/dss-documentation.html) - The DSS documentation specifies implementation and validation of eIDAS signature formats and trust lists. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [DSS Source Repository](https://github.com/esig/dss) - Java framework for creating, extending and validating XAdES, CAdES, PAdES and JAdES advanced electronic signatures against eIDAS trust-service requirements. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [eIDAS Standards and Specifications](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/DIGITAL/pages/467109093/Standards+and+specifications) - The Commission catalogue lists standards used to implement eIDAS electronic signatures and trust services. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [ENISA Overview of Standards Related to eIDAS](https://www.enisa.europa.eu/sites/default/files/publications/ENISA%20Report%20-%20Overview%20of%20standards%20related%20to%20eIDAS.pdf) - ENISA maps technical standards relevant to implementation of eIDAS services. 🇪🇺 `EU/ENISA` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [ETSI EN 319 142-1 PAdES](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/319100_319199/31914201/01.02.01_60/en_31914201v010201p.pdf) - ETSI European Standard specifying the PAdES baseline PDF signature formats used by eIDAS-compliant qualified signature and seal creation tools. 🇪🇺 `EU/ETSI` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [ETSI EN 319 411-1 Trust Service Provider Policy Requirements](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/319400_319499/31941101/01.04.01_60/en_31941101v010401p.pdf) - ETSI European Standard setting policy and security requirements for trust service providers issuing certificates under eIDAS, used in QTSP conformity assessment. 🇪🇺 `EU/ETSI` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [ETSI TR 119 460](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_tr/119400_119499/119460/01.01.01_60/tr_119460v010101p.pdf) - ETSI TR 119 460 provides implementation guidance for eIDAS trust-service validation. 🇪🇺 `EU/ETSI` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [ETSI TS 119 612 Trusted Lists](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/119600_119699/119612/02.03.01_60/ts_119612v020301p.pdf) - ETSI specification defining the format and provisioning rules for the national Trusted Lists of qualified trust service providers mandated by eIDAS. 🇪🇺 `EU/ETSI` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [EU Digital Identity Wallet GitHub Organisation](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet) - The European Commission organisation hosting every European Digital Identity Wallet reference implementation, library and specification. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [EU Trusted List Browser](https://eidas.ec.europa.eu/efda/tl-browser/) - European Commission service for browsing EU and EEA national Trusted Lists and the List of Trusted Lists of qualified trust service providers under eIDAS. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [EUDI Android Wallet Reference Application](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-app-android-wallet-ui) - Reference Android wallet from the EU Digital Identity Wallet organisation implementing OpenID4VCI issuance and OpenID4VP and ISO 18013-5 presentation of PID and mDL credentials. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [EUDI iOS Wallet Reference Application](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-app-ios-wallet-ui) - Reference iOS wallet from the EU Digital Identity Wallet organisation demonstrating credential issuance, storage and presentation as specified by the ARF. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [EUDI SD-JWT VC Library](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-lib-jvm-sdjwt-kt) - Kotlin and JVM library implementing SD-JWT selectively disclosable verifiable credentials for European Digital Identity Wallet issuance and verification flows. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [EUDI Wallet Architecture and Reference Framework](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework) - Technical specification defining the common architecture and functional requirements for the European Digital Identity Wallet under eIDAS 2. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [EUDI Wallet Implementation Portal](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/eudi-wallet-implementation) - The Commission portal provides architecture, reference implementation, and testing resources for EU Digital Identity Wallets. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [EUDIW Credential Issuer Service](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-srv-web-issuing-eudiw-py) - Reference OpenID4VCI credential issuer for PID, mDL and qualified electronic attestations used in European Digital Identity Wallet pilots. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [EUDIW Verifier Endpoint](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-srv-verifier-endpoint) - Reference OpenID4VP verifier and relying-party backend for validating European Digital Identity Wallet credential presentations. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [EWC Consortium](https://github.com/EWC-consortium) - GitHub organisation of the EU Digital Identity Wallet Consortium Large Scale Pilot, hosting conformance test infrastructure, RFCs, rulebooks and reference wallet implementations. 🇪🇺 `EU/EWC Consortium` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [libdigidocpp](https://github.com/open-eid/libdigidocpp) - Estonian C++ library maintained by RIA for creating and verifying XAdES-based signed documents used in Estonia's national eID and eIDAS trust services. 🇪🇪 `Estonia/RIA` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [NOBID Consortium](https://www.nobidconsortium.com/) - Nordic-Baltic eID Large Scale Pilot funded by the Commission, testing European Digital Identity Wallet payment and cross-border eID use cases across eight EU and EEA countries. 🇪🇺 `EU/NOBID Consortium` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [POTENTIAL Consortium](https://www.digital-identity-wallet.eu/) - Commission-funded Large Scale Pilot co-led by France and Germany that tested the European Digital Identity Wallet across government, banking, telecom, mDL, signature and health use cases. 🇪🇺 `EU/POTENTIAL Consortium` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>
- [walt.id Identity](https://github.com/walt-id/waltid-identity) - Austrian open-source issuer, wallet and verifier stack supporting OpenID4VCI, OpenID4VP, SD-JWT VC and mdoc formats used in European Digital Identity Wallet pilots. 🇦🇹 `Austria/walt.id` <sub>Sovereign Identity & Trust (eIDAS)</sub>

- [EUCC Certification Scheme](https://certification.enisa.europa.eu/certification-library/eucc-certification-scheme_en) - EU-wide Common Criteria-based cybersecurity certification scheme for ICT products, established under the Cybersecurity Act by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/482. 🇪🇺 `EU/ENISA` <sub>Governance, Risk & Policy Mapping</sub>

- [EUCS Candidate Cloud Certification Scheme](https://www.enisa.europa.eu/publications/eucs-cloud-service-scheme) - ENISA publishes the candidate EU cybersecurity certification scheme for cloud services. 🇪🇺 `EU/ENISA` <sub>Sovereign Cloud & DevSecOps</sub>
- [SCS Standards and Compliance Test Suite](https://github.com/SovereignCloudStack/standards) - Machine-readable Sovereign Cloud Stack standards and an automated compliance-check suite used to certify European providers as SCS-compatible IaaS or KaaS. 🇩🇪 `Germany/Sovereign Cloud Stack` <sub>Sovereign Cloud & DevSecOps</sub>
- [SecNumCloud](https://cyber.gouv.fr/enjeux-technologiques/cloud/) - ANSSI's SecNumCloud qualification page provides the French reference material for qualified cloud services. 🇫🇷 `France/ANSSI` <sub>Sovereign Cloud & DevSecOps</sub>

- [SOG-IS Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms](https://www.sogis.eu/documents/cc/crypto/SOGIS-Agreed-Cryptographic-Mechanisms-1.3.pdf) - SOG-IS Crypto Working Group document specifying the cryptographic mechanisms accepted for Common Criteria evaluations across participating European states. 🇪🇺 `EU/SOG-IS` <sub>Cryptography, Certification & Post-Quantum Readiness</sub>

- [Besluit veiligheid en integriteit telecommunicatie](https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0042843) - Dutch decree setting binding security and integrity requirements for public electronic communications networks, including the supplier-risk powers of the EU 5G Toolbox. 🇳🇱 `Netherlands/Rijksoverheid` <sub>Telecom, 5G & Network Infrastructure Security</sub>

- [BSI TR-03163 Security in Telecommunications Infrastructure](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/TechGuidelines/TR03163/BSI-TR-03163.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=7) - BSI TR-03163 specifies security requirements for telecommunications infrastructure used in German 5G networks. 🇩🇪 `Germany/BSI` <sub>Telecom, 5G & Network Infrastructure Security</sub>
- [Bundesnetzagentur Katalog von Sicherheitsanforderungen](https://www.bundesnetzagentur.de/DE/Fachthemen/Telekommunikation/OeffentlicheSicherheit/KatalogSicherheitsanforderungen/Katalog_eng.html) - Germany's binding catalogue of telecom security requirements issued by Bundesnetzagentur with the BSI, implementing the EECC security duties in national law. 🇩🇪 `Germany/Bundesnetzagentur` <sub>Telecom, 5G & Network Infrastructure Security</sub>
- [ENISA 5G Security Controls Matrix](https://www.enisa.europa.eu/publications/5g-security-controls-matrix) - ENISA maps 5G threats to security controls supporting implementation of the EU 5G Toolbox. 🇪🇺 `EU/ENISA` <sub>Telecom, 5G & Network Infrastructure Security</sub>
- [ENISA 5G Supplement under the EECC](https://www.enisa.europa.eu/publications/5g-supplement-security-measures-under-eecc) - ENISA specifies security measures for 5G operators under the European Electronic Communications Code. 🇪🇺 `EU/ENISA` <sub>Telecom, 5G & Network Infrastructure Security</sub>
- [ENISA CIRAS](https://ciras.enisa.europa.eu/) - ENISA's Cybersecurity Incident Reporting and Analysis System, where EU telecom regulators submit and explore Article 40 EECC security incident data. 🇪🇺 `EU/ENISA` <sub>Telecom, 5G & Network Infrastructure Security</sub>
- [ENISA Security in 5G Specifications](https://www.enisa.europa.eu/sites/default/files/publications/ENISA%20Report%20-%20Security%20in%205G%20Specifications.pdf) - ENISA analysis of the security controls inside 3GPP 5G standalone specifications, written to guide national regulators setting requirements under the EECC. 🇪🇺 `EU/ENISA` <sub>Telecom, 5G & Network Infrastructure Security</sub>

## Post-quantum transition

*Recommendation (EU) 2024/1101* - 12 entries

- [ANSSI Views on the Post-Quantum Cryptography Transition](https://messervices.cyber.gouv.fr/guides/en-anssi-views-post-quantum-cryptography-transition) - ANSSI position paper setting a phased timeline for migrating French systems to hybrid and then post-quantum cryptography. 🇫🇷 `France/ANSSI` <sub>Cryptography, Certification & Post-Quantum Readiness</sub>
- [CRYSTALS](https://pq-crystals.org/) - Reference implementations of the Kyber KEM and Dilithium signature scheme from a largely European team spanning CWI, ENS Lyon, Radboud University, Ruhr University Bochum and IBM Research Zurich. 🇳🇱 `Netherlands/Radboud University` <sub>Cryptography, Certification & Post-Quantum Readiness</sub>
- [eBACS](https://bench.cr.yp.to/results-sign.html) - Benchmarking site originating in the EU ECRYPT and VAMPIRE projects and run from TU Eindhoven, comparing public-key and post-quantum signature implementations. 🇳🇱 `Netherlands/TU Eindhoven` <sub>Cryptography, Certification & Post-Quantum Readiness</sub>
- [ENISA Post-Quantum Cryptography Report](https://www.enisa.europa.eu/publications/post-quantum-cryptography-current-state-and-quantum-mitigation) - ENISA technical report assessing the standardisation status of post-quantum algorithms and proposing hybrid mitigation strategies for EU organisations. 🇪🇺 `EU/ENISA` <sub>Cryptography, Certification & Post-Quantum Readiness</sub>
- [EuroQCI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/quantum) - European Commission and ESA initiative, signed by all 27 Member States, to build an EU-wide quantum key distribution communication infrastructure. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Cryptography, Certification & Post-Quantum Readiness</sub>
- [FALCON](https://falcon-sign.info/) - Post-quantum signature scheme with a reference implementation from a design team including French researchers, selected for standardisation and tracked in EU migration guidance. 🇫🇷 `France/Multi-institution` <sub>Cryptography, Certification & Post-Quantum Readiness</sub>
- [Kryptografie quantensicher gestalten](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/DE/BSI/Publikationen/Broschueren/Kryptografie-quantensicher-gestalten.html) - BSI publication explaining quantum-computing risk to cryptography and outlining Germany's recommended migration path to quantum-safe algorithms. 🇩🇪 `Germany/BSI` <sub>Cryptography, Certification & Post-Quantum Readiness</sub>
- [PQC Coordinated Implementation Roadmap](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/coordinated-implementation-roadmap-transition-post-quantum-cryptography) - First deliverable of the NIS Cooperation Group's post-quantum work stream, setting milestones from 2026 to 2035 for Member States to migrate critical infrastructure. 🇪🇺 `EU/NIS Cooperation Group` <sub>Cryptography, Certification & Post-Quantum Readiness</sub>
- [PQCRYPTO](https://pqcrypto.eu.org/) - EU Horizon 2020 project coordinated by TU Eindhoven that designed and benchmarked the post-quantum public-key systems underpinning much of the European PQC tooling ecosystem. 🇳🇱 `Netherlands/TU Eindhoven` <sub>Cryptography, Certification & Post-Quantum Readiness</sub>
- [pqm4](https://github.com/mupq/pqm4) - Benchmarking and testing suite from Radboud University, descended from the EU Horizon 2020 PQCRYPTO project, for post-quantum algorithms on ARM Cortex-M4 microcontrollers. 🇳🇱 `Netherlands/Radboud University` <sub>Cryptography, Certification & Post-Quantum Readiness</sub>
- [Recommendation (EU) 2024/1101 on Post-Quantum Cryptography](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/recommendation-coordinated-implementation-roadmap-transition-post-quantum-cryptography) - European Commission recommendation calling on Member States to adopt a coordinated roadmap for moving public administration and critical infrastructure to post-quantum cryptography. 🇪🇺 `EU/European Commission` <sub>Cryptography, Certification & Post-Quantum Readiness</sub>
- [SPHINCS+](https://sphincs.org/) - Stateless hash-based signature scheme led by researchers at TU Eindhoven, Radboud University, MPI-SP and Graz University of Technology, now part of the post-quantum standard set. 🇳🇱 `Netherlands/TU Eindhoven` <sub>Cryptography, Certification & Post-Quantum Readiness</sub>
